grh_829ece093c8807d0331b.title: A Poor Orphan Girl
paragraphs: In 1896, a nearly seventeen-year-old girl takes a job waiting tables so she can earn enough money for a wedding dress and marry local sheriff Harvey. On her first day, aging outlaw Rooster Redleg hides in her room, holds her at gunpoint and forces her to conceal him while Harvey and a posse search town. Once she realizes the famous outlaw is less murderous legend than shabby fugitive, fear gives way to fascination. Desperate for money and adventure, she even proposes joining Rooster as his partner so they can rob together and make their names famous. Rooster refuses and tries to escape, only to be recognized outside. The girl remains behind, returns to her supper shift, and Harvey tells her they will talk afterward about their future together.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on June 4, 1979. It is listed as episode 86 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Sam Edwards, John Larch, Mary Jane Croft, Jack Manning, and Barney Phillips. Other credited names include Percy Grainger as writer.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_823fecb2933b7344b6a4.title: Countess Maritza
paragraphs: Countess Maritza falls in love with Tassilo while believing him to be merely the manager of her estate, but the romance collapses when she learns that he has concealed his true social position and begins to fear that he wants her fortune. Tassilo refuses to defend himself and prepares to leave. His sister Liza tells Maritza that he truly loves her and could easily marry another wealthy woman if money were his object. grh_826f67898da9cf0d7119.title: The Sybil of Sycamore Lane
paragraphs: Suburban housewife Kate begins to believe she is clairvoyant after a series of accurate hunches, including calling her children away just before a dangerous object crashes where they were playing and tipping a friend to a profitable stock. Her skeptical husband Adam grows uneasy when the gift intrudes into his work and their marriage. A deliberately confident weather prediction finally fails during a picnic, and Adam discovers that the stock tip could have come from information Kate overheard. Their tension eases, though Kate ends the story still convinced she has at least a little intuition left.

grh_82511bc3dd05f71be114.title: The Time for Decision-U.s.War Aims
paragraphs: A policy-focused dramatization drawing on Sumner Welles's The Time for Decision and Walter Lippmann's U.S. War Aims asks what kind of peace can prevent another world war. Through family scenes, historical comparisons and direct argument, it warns that military victory alone will fail if nations return to isolation, power politics and unresolved rivalries. The broadcast urges Americans to study competing plans for international security and decide whether the next generation will inherit a durable peace or an even more destructive war.
